journey.title: Take a scenario from source to an installable Android app
journey.purpose: The primary loop. An owner picks a scenario, generates an Android app, proves it behaves correctly, and learns exactly what remains before a person can install it. The journey must be completable on a host with no Android SDK and no Play account — ending honestly at a named blocker rather than a failure.

steps.intent: Start from a state with no generated project and understand that generating one is the next step.
See the probed target matrix and recognise which targets can actually be proven on this host.
Understand precisely why the emulator target is unavailable and what would resolve it.
With the toolchain present, start a validation run over the selected cells.
Read the conformance chapters and confirm the generated app satisfies the Android platform contract.
Learn that the artifact is proven but not shippable, see the first concrete action and its cost, and see the dated obligations that constrain it.

claims.statement: The full journey is walkable with no Play Console account, ending at a named blocking rung rather than an error.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-009. An owner must be able to prove their app works before spending money on distribution. A flow that dead-ends on a missing account conflates validation with release.

claims.statement: From the matrix, the reason a target is unavailable is reachable in a single navigation.
claims.rationale: S2A-P0-003. If diagnosing an unavailable target requires the CLI, the operator surface has failed at its main job.

claims.statement: A fully passing matrix never presents itself as ready to ship while release readiness rungs are unsatisfied.
claims.rationale: The two axes are independent. Conflating them is how an owner discovers at upload time that they cannot publish.
